stem: A 16-year-old with ADHD describes impulsive sexual decisions that they later regret; what is the best interpretation?

options.text: ADHD is unlikely to be relevant because risky sexual behaviour is determined by relationship status alone
ADHD can exacerbate risky sexual behaviour because conditions that increase impulsivity may worsen this vulnerability
ADHD protects against risky sexual behaviour because it usually delays sexual activity
ADHD matters only if the adolescent is younger than 14 years old
ADHD is relevant only when there is already a confirmed STI

explanation: ADHD can exacerbate risky sexual behaviour. Conditions that increase impulsivity may worsen this vulnerability, so ADHD is clinically relevant in this scenario.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because risky sexual behaviour is not determined by relationship status alone, and ADHD can still be relevant.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because conditions that increase impulsivity may worsen vulnerability to risky sexual behaviour in adolescents with ADHD.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because ADHD is not protective against risky sexual behaviour in this context.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the relevance of ADHD is not limited to adolescents younger than 14 years old.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because ADHD can be relevant as a vulnerability factor even without a confirmed STI.
